utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, this is the statement of your colleague, Mr. Abrahams, that I read to you a moment ago. I simply want you to be able to see that statement for yourself. Thank you, that's the correct page. You can see, Mr. Bouckaert, at the top of the page the exchange between counsel at the top of the page. It asks this of your colleague: "Do you happen to know what the position of your organisation or your former organisation is, sir, for releasing this information," to which Mr. Abrahams said: "I do". "And what is that position"? And that is the passage I read out to you: "As a matter of policy, the notes are the private property of the organisation, but individuals or organisation can make specific request to our legal office for a release which will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis." I simply wanted to read it out to you since I told you I would come back to it. Is that correct, sir, and simply to clarify an answer you gave to me earlier on today, that on any mission that you undertake, there would be a significant amount of information that would be withdrawn or taken out from your report either because you consider it to be unreliable or because you were unable to find corroboration for that material; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I would simply ask you about one particular report which you prepared yourself most recently, which concerned the bombing of South Lebanon by Israel. It relates to a matter of methodology which will later be relevant, but is that correct that one of the issues which you had to determine in this report is whether targeting by Israeli forces was indiscriminate or whether they were, in fact, aiming at Hezbollah positions; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I believe, and correct me if I'm wrong, that you visited a number of locations which had received Israeli fighter -- fire, I'm sorry, to determine whether in fact there had been a Hezbollah position or a Hezbollah presence in the area at the time?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, and coming to the Court to give this testimony has interrupted a finalisation of the report on those issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise, at least on the part of the Defence, but the questions will be short in relation to this report. Is that correct also that for each incident or alleged incidents of targeting by the Israeli forces of the Hezbollah, you sought to obtain witness from outside the area controlled by the Hezbollah to corroborate the version which was given to you?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe you're talking about the Fatal Strikes report.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That report was compiled during the time that the conflict was still ongoing, so our access to both locations and witnesses was extremely limited.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that for each incident of alleged indiscriminate targeting, you would insist to find corroboration by eyewitnesses or otherwise outside of areas controlled by the Hezbollah to ensure the reliability of the evidence?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but it was often difficult to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that when you were unable to do so, you would drop the particular incident from your report?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you did not put the onus on the Israeli government to demonstrate to your satisfaction that there was, in fact, no Hezbollah position in those particular locations; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, although we did ask the Israeli government for information about the intelligence that they had relating to particular strikes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If you did not put the onus you to produce evidence and material that they were positioned there? Hezbollah --

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: -- positions. Thank you. Is that correct that in tense circumstances, such as conflict situations, be it in Israel or in other parts of the world, it's very important for you to get the full picture of what's going on before you report about it; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also correct that this full picture means that you would have to hear from both sides of that conflict or situation?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I would simply ask -- or I would read out to you a statement made by your colleague, Mr. Abrahams, again in the context of the Milatinovic proceedings, and that would be 1D428 with an ERN 1D00-3919 to 1D00-3920. Mr. Bouckaert, I'll draw your attention to the bottom of the page, if it can be enlarged, thank you, and a bit for Mr. Bouckaert, and that would be at the bottom of the page. Your colleague, Mr. Abrahams, was being asked by Defence counsel Ivetic the following: "You would agree, would you not, that in order to have a full and complete picture in any circumstance it is always preferred or in fact even essential to hear both sides in a conflict, is it not?" And if we turn to the next page, it will be on the top of the next page. Mr. Abrahams answered: "Yes." And that's, I suppose, a conclusion you would agree with.

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say it's always preferred, yes, but it's not always possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it also correct, Mr. Bouckaert, that the accuracy and the reliability of any of your reporting would be not only dependent but also greatly enhanced by the fact that you have talked to both sides?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly, but we feel that the position of Mr. Boskoski and the government was reflected in our report based on public statements made by him and by the government.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But in general terms, you would agree with the proposition that your findings would have been much weakened by the fact that you had only talked to one side, to put it that way?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I would not agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let me ask the Registry to show what is 1D428. That's ERN 1D0031 -- sorry, 3910 to 1D00-3911, and it's again taken from the Milatinovic proceedings. And the witness in this case was again was a Mr. Abrahams, and it's dated the 7th of August of 2006, and the page is 983 and 984. If we can scroll down a little bit to the bottom of the page, please. If I may draw your attention, Mr. Bouckaert, to that last part of that document of that page with the questions that -- okay. With the question which says: "Now, would it be fair to say, then, that your reports were generated without any information or input from the Yugoslav or Serbian authorities?" And if we can turn to the next page, this is the answer of Mr. Abrahams: "I would not say that's fair to say. We used open source material wherever possible to present the government view, and I sincerely wish that we had received responses to these letters from one of the many agencies and ministries to whom they were sent, to which they were sent, because I would have -- the report would have been strengthened greatly and all our work would have been strengthened greatly by having official answers to these particular inquiries. Would you then agree with the proposition made by Mr. Abrahams?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I certainly agree it would have strengthened -- it would strengthen any report to reflect information obtained from the government.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: And that's something we strive to do in all of our reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, in fact, it's your usual practice to send a request of that nature to the authorities for information; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not characterise it as our usual practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, would you characterise it, then, as your usual operating procedure; would that be fair?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I would say it's a common practice, but we take into account working conditions, security concerns, to make that kind of evaluation.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown it's 1D424, and it's again a transcript from the Milatinovic proceedings of 14 July 2006. The ERN is 1D003805. It's from the 14th of July of 2006.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Abrahams is talking about the letters which he sent to the Serbian and Yugoslav authorities, and he's being asked by Counsel Stepaniuk: "Whether this letter, was it your idea to send this letter?" And the answer of Mr. Abrahams, you can see it in the middle of the page, he says: "This letter is standard operating procedure following a mission to request information from the government." Do you agree with that statement?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've already testified, I think it's a common operating procedure. I would not characterise it as standard. To the extent possible, we do try to send requests of information to the government, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you've explained that in the case of Ljuboten, you did not do so; is that --

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you did it in other -- I mean, you've mentioned the issue of security, and I will come back to that, but is that correct that you sent such request for information --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please slow down for the interpreters and make breaks between questions and answers. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You've mentioned, Mr. Bouckaert, the fact that security issues were a fact relevant to your procedures in that respect. Is that correct that in a number of conflict situations characterised as quite dangerous places, you have, in fact, followed the procedure outlined by Mr. Abrahams of sending letters of inquiries to various governments; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You've done that, for instance, in relation to the events of Kosovo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and more recently to Israel about the events in Lebanon.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you've also done that, for instance, in Sri Lanka in relation to one of your reports concerning abduction and child recruitment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not one of my reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But it's been done by your organisation; are you aware of that or not?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly, but I also have just came back from the Central African Republic, and we didn't send such a request for information. I just came back from Somalia, and we didn't send such a request for information, so it's certainly not done in every case.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you've done it also, for instance, in your report --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please make breaks.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: -- called "Hearts and Minds, Post-War Seen in Baghdad caused by US Forces;" is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not one of my reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So you are not aware of the fact of whether or not it was done?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that case I do believe that it was done, because it was a report dealing with US military abuses, and we have had good cooperation from the US military on getting credible information from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It was also the practice of your organisation, when possible, to contact either NGOs or international organisations which were on the ground in the relevant area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the reason for doing so again was to verify the reliability and accuracy of the information which you had obtained; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I think in your statement, Mr. Bouckaert, you mention talking to one OSCE observer which you don't identify, but is that correct, you talked to one particular OSCE observer?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you refer to where I say this in my statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I believe it's in your report. What I'm going to ask you is this: Did you make any requests to the OSCE for official information at the time you speak of in your report?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did discuss our findings with OSCE officials.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you recall with whom of the -- which official of the OSCE did you discuss that matter?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was either Sandra Mitchell or Mr. Bolton.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will read out your statement, Mr. Bouckaert. It's at page 18 of the report, and you refer to one of the OSCE monitors speaking on condition of anonymity. It's P352, it's been identified, but the sentence goes on to say that it confirmed to the Associated Press that the OSCE have found the remains of five persons in the village. What I'm trying to ascertain, Mr. Bouckaert, is whether or not you actually talked to any representative of the OSCE in Macedonia at the time when you were there.

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, I would just like to see the reference from the --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It is at the top of the page, page 18 of your report.

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a reference to the OSCE speaking on condition of anonymity to the Associated Press, not to Human Rights Watch.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you talk to any representative of the OSCE in Macedonia at the time?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you identify that individual, that person?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, it was either Sandra Mitchell or Mr. Bolton or both.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you contact any other international organisation or NGO which was on the ground at the time?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We had very regular discussions with a number of organisations, including UNHCR, as well as the ICRC.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you contact any of these organisations or NGOs in relation to the events at Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did discuss the events of Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you obtain official information from any of those organisations in relation to these events?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, these were informal discussions.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it also the practice of your organisation, sir, to obtain information not only from the authorities but directly from the people who you consider to be the perpetrators or the people responsible for violations of IHL?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: On some occasions, we have done such investigations and such interviews.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that the usual practice, sir, or is that something that is done rarely?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say it's a rare practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you didn't do that in the case of the Ljuboten; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I'm just pausing to allow for the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful for your assistance. Is that also correct, Mr. Bouckaert, that it's quite an exceptional practice for your organisation to actually name an individual who you consider to be responsible for violations of IHL?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's -- we name individuals if we have clear and convincing information that they are linked directly to IHL violations, including quite a few people who are in the custody of this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That would be my next question. Apart from your Kosovo reports and the Ljuboten reports, is there any other report of Human Rights Watch which, so to say, point the finger at any individual as being responsible for a violation of IHL?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of IHL or human rights abuses as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I mean IHL.

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I certainly have written reports where we named officials for issues of torture, for example, in Azerbaijan, but those were not conflict related, and I'm working on a report about a Central African which may name some individuals. And in Sri Lanka, we named the head of the Korina [phoen] Group as responsible for the abduction of children, forced recruitment of children.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that this is the practice of Human Rights Watch not to name or not to point the finger at anyone in that manner unless you have three independent sources, at least, to back your claim; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of the rule requiring three independent sources. Our counsel in the case of a report that would name individuals would more carefully review those reports to ensure that we had adequate information and convincing information to make those charges.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I'll show what is 1D427. It's ERN 1D004073. So this is one of the reports which I understand you've contributed to is "Under Orders, War Crimes in Kosovo," is that correct, you contributed to that report?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I contributed research, but not writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I would like to read to you a passage. It's at Roman XXII in the introduction section. I am just waiting for this document to appear. It's Rule 65 ter 1D427 with an ERN of 1D00-4053. And that's the "7" which is on my piece of paper as, in fact, a "1", it could be 1D421. I'll read to you in the meantime, Mr. Bouckaert, what the document says. It's not the correct document that appears. I'll read it out to you. This is page 22 of the introduction of this report. It says this: "The naming of alleged perpetrators was undertaken with particular care, although Kosovar Albanians often did not know their tormentors, a few names are mentioned in this report. For each, at least three independent sources confirm their participation in a crime." So I suppose what I'm asking you is whether that was common practice for Human Rights Watch to have a requirement of three minimum sources for each identification of alleged perpetrators or whether the practice varied depending on the report.

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've said, our reports are -- if we're going to name any individuals, counsel will make a determination that we have adequate and convincing evidence. I think in the case of "Under Orders," which does name a number of perpetrators, this is a descriptive passage of what is contained in that report rather than a description of our standard operating procedures.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would that mean that in some circumstances your organisation would be satisfied to make such a finding with less evidence rather than more or less sources rather than more?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would require adequate and convincing evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that assessment, sir, could you tell the Chamber by whom it would be made, in particular, in relation to Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would have been a central concern of all of the people who reviewed the report, including the Executive Director of the Europe and Central Asia Division, the counsel of Human Rights Watch who would have the primary responsibility in this case, and as well as the official within the Programme Division of Human Rights Watch.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that before making those allegations, you would generally side on the side of caution; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But in the case of the Ljuboten reports, you made the finding that Mr. Boskoski had been intimately involved in the operation and that crimes had been committed by individuals under his authority; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that's the language of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But is that the language you used in the interviews with "The New York Times," for instance, or in the letter which you drafted for Mr. Cartner?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you want to put those in front of me, I'm perfectly happy to review them.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But out of memory, Mr. Bouckaert, is that correct --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, may I object?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You may, but not successfully.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Then I will not, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our report concludes that, by his own admission, Mr. Boskoski was present at Ljuboten during the worst day of the operations there, when -- a day on which we -- our investigation shows crimes were committed, and we asked for his role to be investigated.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: When -- in fairness to you, Mr. Bouckaert, I will read out from you the passage which is attributed to you by "The New York Times." It's P357. It's now admitted in evidence. I apologise. That would be P356. And if I can ask the Registry to focus on the bottom right-hand corner of the document and to enlarge it a bit for Mr. Bouckaert. This is what is recorded as your statement, Mr. Bouckaert: "It's important to understand that he doesn't," and that's Mr. Boskoski, "have to witness the people being killed to have some responsibility for what happened, said Peter Bouckaert, a senior researcher for Human Rights Watch who wrote the group's report on Ljuboten." And then there's another quote which is attributed to you: "It was done by troops under his authority in an action in which he was intimately involved." Can you see that? It's on the top of the next page, perhaps, if the Registry could assist.

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And does that accurately reflect what you recall saying to Mr. Fisher, the journalist?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Fisher wrote -- read Mr. Boskoski's quote to me and asked me to respond to it, so it's in direct response to Mr. Boskoski's statement. And I think it's an accurate summary of the law of command responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm simply asking you to state whether that's an accurate representation of what you told the journalist, Mr. Bouckaert.

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness now please be shown MA5353. It's a "P" number.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that, you explained, is a letter which you drafted for Ms. Anderson and which was signed by or in any case adopted by her; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I may draw your attention to a paragraph, it's the third paragraph from the bottom of that page which starts with the words: "The Macedonian government ..." Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in that letter, you say the following: "The Macedonian government must answer to the people of Ljuboten, said Elizabeth Anderson. It is deeply disturbing that the Ministry of Interior appears to have been so intimately involved in one of the worst abuses of the war. We demand an impartial investigation." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that was the nature of your conclusion as to what you believe or understood Mr. Boskoski to have done or partaken in at the time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You've explained to the Prosecution and earlier in your evidence the reasons why you did not send a letter of inquiry to the Ministry of Interior, and you explained that you had security concerns; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was one of the reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And could you state what the other reasons were?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the Ministry had already made public many statements about what happened in Ljuboten, and we were not certain that we would get any credible or relevant information from them if we did ask them.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So it was your understanding that the Ministry could not have assisted you in relation to your investigation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that's overstating it a little bit. We would have reviewed any information they would have provided us for it. We just didn't believe that we would get much -- much credible or relevant information from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you've indicated that you had some security concerns. Is that correct that you did not receive any threats at the time?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not receive any personal threats, but I certainly had many -- several incidents where police officials acted towards me in a very hostile manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you were not threatened or otherwise physically abused; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And there was no interference with your work from the Ministry of Interior; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, were you allowed to enter the village on the 23rd of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you were not searched when you entered, or were you, when you went out of the village at that time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: My car was searched when entered the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And none of your belongings or notebooks or cameras were taken from you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And no one came to confiscate your notes at your hotel during that period between the 17th and the 25th of August; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And no one sought to detain or arrest you or search you for this information at the airport when you left Macedonia on the 26th or 27th; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And your pass with the Ministry of Information was never revoked; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you were again allowed to travel freely to Macedonia whenever you wished, and I understood you returned to Macedonia, if only in passing, at later days. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, in passing.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also correct that you've described your relationship with the Ministry of Interior as being a good one; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you tell me what you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, do you recall giving an interview to any newspaper where you were asked about the nature of your relationship with the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Macedonian press?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did give such an interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you recall also being asked about the nature of your relationship with the Ministry of Interior and the Macedonians' authority in general?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't recall what my exact answer was, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But do you recall indicating to the journalist that, in fact, your relationship with the government of Macedonia at the time was a fruitful one?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but because what we wanted to encourage through this interview is a dialogue with the Macedonian government, and I stressed in the interview that we were not against ethnic Macedonians, that we were not against the Macedonian government, that our mandate was simply to stop the human rights abuses, because we did face a lot of hostility from both the local population and from some elements of the government.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that you also told the journalist that you were [realtime read in error"weren't"] taken seriously by the government; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: By some elements of the government.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that you also said that you had many constructive meetings with government representatives?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: With some government representatives.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that you also received answers in detail to issues which you had raised with government representatives?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, although not through official channels.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that, in fact at the time when you were interviewed, you indicated that the assistance which you received from the government was fruitful, as I mentioned, but that your complaints were directed to the problems which you encountered in the field? Is that correct, is that what you told the journalist?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I mean, this is an interview which was given six years ago, and I can't recall the exact details.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I can help you here, Mr. Bouckaert. I believe it's Rule 65 ter 324. It has an ERN range of N002-5309, N002-5313-80 for the English, and the Macedonian version starts at N002-5309. Your Honour, before starting again with the questions, there's a line 4 and 5 of page 68 where I'm recorded as asking Mr. Bouckaert: "Is that correct that you also told the journalist that you weren't, were not, taken seriously by the government," whereas the question or at least as I put it was that: "You were taken seriously by the government," so I'll simply ask Mr. Bouckaert again, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct, Mr. Bouckaert, that you told the journalist at that time that you were taken seriously by the government?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had serious discussions with elements of the government.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, at least on the English version, I don't see a date for this article. I'm wondering whether we can simply be informed the date of this publication or the date of the interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Certainly. We understand the article having been given by Mr. Bouckaert in July of 2001. Mr. Bouckaert may confirm that, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, do you recall -- you have the article now in front of you, it was with Anna Petruseva [phoen], can you recall that conversation?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall the conversation. I just don't recall the details of the questions or the answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall that this conversation took place sometime in the month of July of 2001?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, or -- I don't know, actually, the exact date. It was definitely after the events in Aracinovo, because the picture is from Aracinovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it was sometimes in the summer of 2001; is that --

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can turn to the third page of that document, it's N002-5311-80. There's a question put to you by the journalist in the following terms: "How do you evaluate the cooperation with the Macedonian authorities? Is there a feeling for the problems that you indicate?" And that's your answer as recorded: "We have a fruitful cooperation at the government level. I have an impression that our indications are being considered really seriously. We have had many constructive meetings with government representatives and received answers in detail about the case we pointed out. However, the situation in the field is somewhat different. For example, we know that many foreign journalists face the problem of check-points. Members of the police and the army are undisciplined. We have many times encountered drunken soldiers and policemen." Is that an accurate record of what you recall saying to this journalist?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I can't vouch for the accuracy, especially of the part where it says "we have received answers in detail about the cases we pointed out," because either at that stage or a later stage, that certainly wasn't the case. So I don't know if it's a problem of translation or of an inaccurate reflection in the original, but that part certainly I don't feel is accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So you are suggesting that you didn't say that to the journalist at the time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, because I don't recall having received any answers in detail about the cases we discussed with the government, so yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So is that the case of you not remembering receiving those information or you're not telling the journalist this fact?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I think it's an inaccurate reflection of the interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also correct, Mr. Bouckaert, that originally when you were asked about the reasons why you had not given an opportunity to Mr. Boskoski to communicate with you, you had different -- you had given quite a different explanation than the one you gave yesterday and today?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall telling the journalists that -- when asked that particular question, that you had tried but that Mr. Boskoski was away from Macedonia at the time?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never tried to contact Mr. Boskoski.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown what is Rule 65 ter 1D380. It has an ERN of 1D00-3573. And the Macedonian version is 1D00-3572.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, what will appear in front of you is, on the right-hand side, an excerpt of a press article from "Dnevnik" and on the left you'll have the English translation of that same article. It's dated the 29th of August, 2001, and the headline is: "Boskoski Human Rights Watch Hideously Distorts the Truth." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: M'mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then it refers to: "Peter Bouckaert, a senior researcher with the Human Rights Watch protection organisation, Human Rights Watch," can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And "Dnevnik" says--

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Kindly slow down for the benefit of the transcript and the interpreters. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It says: "Peter Bouckaert confirmed yesterday for Dnevnik that his report would contain serious accusations against the Minister of the Interior, Ljube Boskoski." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it goes on to say: "In Bouckaret's words, the report will state that several civilians were killed in the operation by the Macedonian security forces which allegedly was led by Boskoski in the village of Ljuboten in the Skopje area." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then there's a quote again attributed to you further down which says: "We are convinced that the persons killed in Ljuboten were civilians, and this judgement is based on the evidence available to us. We have not found one single piece of evidence to suggest that they were terrorists. We found only civilian clothing, and there was no indications of the presence of the NLA in the area. In the course of our investigation, we spoke with local people, international observers and the Macedonian authorities, but we are unable to speak with the Minister of the Interior since he was out of the country when we tried to meet him,' Bouckaert said." Is that what you told the journalist at "Dnevnik" Mr. Bouckaert? ?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall giving this interview but it's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall telling the journalist at the time that you had been unable to contact Mr. Boskoski because he was out of the country at the time?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't recall giving the interview so I don't recall making that statement, and I don't even recall knowing that Boskoski had been out of the country at the time. He certainly appeared on the news the night before this report was made.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So you are saying that is -- it is again a case of the journalist having either invented stories or attributed statements to you that --

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: -- you didn't make?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm just saying I don't recall giving this particular interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But are you suggesting it did not happen or --

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I just don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Okay. Well, Your Honour, perhaps we'll seek to tender this document at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Again, what's the relevance? We have quoted into the transcript the passage that you want, the date of the article.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: In that case, we won't insist, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But is that correct, Mr. Bouckaert, that you also could have sent a fax or a letter to the Minister of the Interior once you had returned in New York; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we could have.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you didn't do it?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if we had the fax number for the Minister of Interior -- Ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you didn't seek to find that number, and in fact you never sent a fax and never gave a call to the Ministry; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, I focused on writing up my findings.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct also that that was again basic Human Rights Watch practice, to contact or proceed to contact authorities upon return from a mission?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, as I think I've stated previously, it's a common practice. It's certainly not a practice that we engage in every case and this was discussed with my superiors, and we decided not to do it in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, again, the reason for it, that you didn't believe that any meaningful information could be provided to you by the Ministry; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, that on the 29th of August, 2001, the Ministry of Interior in fact wrote a letter to Holly Cartner, your superior, I understand, asking you to contact the Ministry; is that something which is within your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it within your knowledge that the Defence of the co-accused Mr. Tarculovski sent a number of requests to your organisation for information and assistance?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct, sir, that a large part of your report, in particular as concern Mr. Boskoski, is based on media report or, more precisely, a television broadcast?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that television broadcast has about two lines in the report. It does -- yes, it is mentioned that there was a television broadcast of which we obtained a copy that showed Mr. Boskoski in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps we'll turn then to -- it's P352, it's [inaudible], it's again your report, and I will ask the Registry to turn to page 15 of that report. Sorry, that would be two pages further. That's the 15th page in the report, so that means the 17th page. Yes, thank you, that's the one. If I may ask you to look at the section under the subheading: "The responsibility of the security forces and the role of the Ministry of Interior, Ljube Boskoski." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And this section is essentially made of three paragraphs; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the only reference, footnotes or authority given in that section is to an MTV newscast on 12th of August of 2001; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also correct, Mr. Bouckaert, that you did not seek to contact the television or the journalist which had prepared that broadcast?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So the evidence or the material upon which you relied in relation to this was, in effect, unverified; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I obtained it from another journalist at MTV.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you didn't query with the person who had done that report whether the content of that material was accurate or not; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: We believed it to be accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you did not verify it?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was rather self-explanatory what the content showed.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct also that you alleged that Mr. Boskoski had been present during the entire operation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We quote the state television newscast as saying that Mr. Boskoski was present during the entire operation, and we say later on that Mr. Boskoski has acknowledged that he was present at Ljuboten on Sunday, but maintains that he arrived at around 4.00 p.m. after the operation was over.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you are aware, sir, of the Macedonian media, not necessarily very reliable; is that something you're aware of?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Boskoski himself has never challenged that he was filmed in Ljuboten on that day, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm just asking you a general question about the reliability of the media or otherwise in Macedonia. Would you agree that they are not always very reliable; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm certainly -- it depends on what they're reporting, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it also correct --

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were often misrepresented in the official state media.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that they were prone to distortion or exaggeration?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: In some cases, yes, including in relation to the work of Human Rights Watch.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also correct that Human Rights Watch would be very careful, as a matter of policy, only to rely -- first rely very carefully on media and only if you knew those media to be sufficiently reliable; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Given the fact that Mr. Boskoski himself never challenged this footage, we remain of the opinion that there is no question as to the reliability of the newscasts that we relied on in this particular case.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But isn't that right that you published the report before Mr. Boskoski was even given a chance to react upon what you wrote in your report? You didn't show him a copy of your report prior to publication; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Boskoski actually did react to this particular information which was contained in "The Sunday Telegraph" story which he reacted to on television that evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But just about yourself, Mr. Bouckaert, if I may, you did not send a copy of your report to Mr. Boskoski, prior to publication, asking for his comment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it's also correct that your organisation would normally not rely upon any media unless those media were, to put it that way, the most reputable and that you would be aware of their work and methodology; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: And we evaluate every piece of evidence on an individual basis, and so it's not like we have a standard set of 12 rules that we apply on whether we include evidence or not. The evidence is evaluated based on an individual basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, can we say this, then: Is that correct that your organisation would, in principle, be relatively wary of relying upon media reports if it could not get access to the primary source?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you still talking about the MTV broadcast or have you --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm speaking of the media in general, Mr. Bouckaert.

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's very difficult to answer these questions in the abstract.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let's take the example of Macedonia there. Would it be correct that you would be very careful -- your organisation would be very careful in the Balkans, in general, when relying upon media reports without any corroboration for information released in the media; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. I have a whole chapter in the report I wrote, "A Week of Terror in Drenica" which about a massacre in Kosovo which talks about the response and the misrepresentations in the official state media of that massacre.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So your answer is "yes"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are careful about the reliability of all information that we include in our reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that also correct that it's the practice of your organisation to rely, in principle, solely on what you consider to be reputable media outlets?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I believe I've answered this question over and over again. In principle, we rely on reliable, reputable media outlets, but we evaluate each piece of evidence based on an individual determination of the reliability and the value of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And was it your position that MTV, the Macedonian Television, was one of those reputable and reliable media outlets?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends what kind of information they're reporting. On issues of abuses against ethnic Albanians, probably not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So your evidence is that they are reliable in part; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And for us, the fact that the national television had shown a minister in the national government on location with police officers, surrounded by police officers, in Ljuboten village while the sounds of gunfire could be heard on the background did give reliability to this particular piece of evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And was it also enough for your organisation to support your statements that Mr. Boskoski had been intimately involved in the operation and that the people who committed the crime had been under his authority? Perhaps I can start with the "intimately involved." Was the press report sufficient for you to make that finding?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think our report and our research is sufficient to make that finding.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, my question is slightly different. My question is whether the report on which you rely, that's the MTV report, was considered by you to be sufficiently reliable to base this finding.

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: We believe it was, my organisation believes it was, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. Is that correct, sir, that you did not talk to any member of the Ministry of Interior or any member of the army which had been involved in the events of the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it also correct that it's the policy of your organisation, its practice, never to rely upon media reports to make allegations about crimes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: In terms of the investigations we carry out, those are carried out by interviewing eyewitnesses as to what they saw committed, and we would not issue reports based solely on media reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct, again, that you would not make an allegation about the commission of a crime by anyone unless -- I mean, based solely on information on media reports; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly, our allegations about Mr. Boskoski are not based solely on media accounts.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, did you talk -- I've asked you already whether you talked to anyone who had been present in the village at the time. Did you talk to anyone who claimed to have been present with Mr. Boskoski in Ljuboten at the time?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but Mr. Boskoski has never denied being in Ljuboten at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, the question perhaps should be better put to you like this: Is that correct that, as I showed you earlier, the part of your report which concerned the alleged responsibility of Mr. Boskoski is based solely on the report from MTV, or is that your evidence that you received any other information or any other evidence which would support your finding that Mr. Boskoski had been intimately involved in the operation?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no evidence for -- available to us to suggest that Mr. Boskoski was not present at Ljuboten on the 12th. He was surrounded by a group of police officers in uniform while the fighting was still taking place, and we found that his presence on August 12th, the day where the most serious abuses in Ljuboten took place, required investigation, and that's our position.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So your position, to understand it properly, is the expression "intimately involved" which you used is no more than an expression to point out the fact that Mr. Boskoski had been present in Ljubanci on the 12th of August; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, that's your evidence; yes?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I think it's quite clear that his role was not limited to just being present, that his presence at the scene in Ljuboten on August 12th suggested that he had played a role in the operation and that's what we wanted to have investigated. We had established that crimes were committed in Ljuboten. The evidence available to us indicated that Mr. Boskoski had been present during the operation while, gunfire was still taking place, surrounded by his commandants, so we felt that his role should be investigated. It was a clear indication that he had played a direct role in the Ljuboten operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So is that correct that you had no evidence of that, you merely assumed it; is that correct, that's what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's a fair assumption based on the evidence that was available to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the evidence is a video footage of his presence at Ljuboten; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: And we didn't have any contradictory evidence to suggest Mr. Boskoski had not been there. I discussed informally our findings with Mr. Stevo Penarovski who was at the time the security adviser to the President and briefed him on our findings, and he certainly didn't make -- show any indication to suggest that Mr. Boskoski had not been there.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But he didn't give you any evidence that he had; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As I said, he gave us no contradictory evidence to suggest that we -- our concerns were somehow unfounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct also that this is not the only occasion when you relied upon press reports to make relatively serious allegations against Mr. Boskoski?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm -- that's a very broad question. I'm -- we did use press accounts to follow Mr. Boskoski's involvement with paramilitary groups, because there was a very difficult issue to investigate, and it was basically the only information which was available to us came from press accounts.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you were happy to forward these allegations, these rumours, which you read from the press; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Forward to who?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, you were content, if I may put it in that way, to propagate those allegations and rumours which you read in the press to other people or other entities; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: We never made those kind of allegations in any public way. I do think I referred to them in my statement to this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I'll direct you to your statement in that case. This is now P322, and I would ask the Registry to go to page 4. That's paragraph 16, 1-6.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Would it be helpful to provide the witness with a copy of his statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, are you able to read it on the screen or would you like --

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If it could be enlarged a bit for Mr. Bouckaert, please. That's paragraph 16, 1-6.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd like to draw your attention, Mr. Bouckaert, to a particular statement which is attributed to you in this statement at the end of the page with the sentence starting: "During the summer months ..." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You're recorded as saying: "During the summer months, Mr. Boskoski personally organised an irregular police unit called The Lions." And then you go on to say: "The Lions were personally --" If we can turn to the next page: "The Lions were personally selected by Mr. Boskoski. After the conflict The Lions briefly blockaded roads when Mr. Boskoski's successor as Minister of Interior attempted to disband the unit. During the conflict, it became publicly known that The Lions had employment contracts not with the Ministry of Interior but with Mr. Boskoski directly." Is that an accurate portrayal of what you told the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And during my proofing, I actually raised some concerns about the phrasing of this paragraph. I wanted to make it clear that I was relying on press accounts in this case. So I would like, for the record, to say that these -- the allegations in this paragraph are based on the information that we received from the press, both before and after the conflict, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And simply for the record, you have indeed corrected your statement, replacing the word "during the conflict" by "after the conflict"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I felt that the paragraph, as written, didn't adequately reflect the fact that it was based on my impression, my following of press accounts, rather than any direct knowledge of myself. So I was concerned about the language of that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that clarification, Mr. Bouckaert. Is that correct also that you actually never verified whether there was any truth in those press reports?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a marginal issue of concern to us, because it was more of a security issue rather than a human rights issue. We were concerned about The Lions because of our knowledge of what paramilitary groups like The Lions had done in other countries -- in other conflicts, like Kosovo and Bosnia, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But with concern back to the statement, Mr. Bouckaert, is that correct that you never sought to verify and that you, in fact, never verified that any of those facts or statements which you gathered from the press were accurate or otherwise?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do believe them to be accurate. There certainly was a unit known as The Lions. They appeared often on television. The question was about their relationship to Mr. Boskoski, and as I explained to you, that was a question of marginal importance to us. We were more focused on documenting human rights abuses rather than on documenting that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So is that your evidence, would that be correct to suggest that other than your awareness of the existence of The Lions unit at some stage, you cannot vouch for the accuracy or reliability of the information stated in that paragraph which I've read to you; is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information contained in that paragraph is based on my following of the press accounts about Mr. Boskoski's links to The Lions. I do believe those press accounts to be accurate, but I do feel that the paragraph, as written, does not reflect the fact that it is simply my opinion based on my reading of the press accounts, yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would it be a convenient time, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Mettraux. Could the Chamber indicate that it would be valuable if we could finish this evening between a quarter to and 10 to 7.00. Is that going to produce any --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: No, not at all, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- great problem? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, I would simply like to read once again the paragraph from your statement. It's paragraph 16. I will just read it to refresh your memory a bit. This is what you are recorded as saying: "Mr. Boskoski, the Macedonian Minister of Interior played a direct role in creating irregular police unit under his direct command. In the summer months, Mr. Boskoski personally organised an irregular police unit called 'The Lions'. The Lions were personally selected by Mr. Boskoski. After the conflict, The Lions briefly blockaded roads when Mr. Boskoski's successor as Minister of the Interior attempted to disband the unit." Then you've corrected the first word, you now say: "After the conflict it became publicly known that The Lions had employment contracts not with the Ministry of the Interior but with Mr. Boskoski directly." And you've adopted that evidence a short while ago. Now, can I ask you this: Have you ever seen any of the official documentation which related to the creation of setting up of The Lions unit?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Have you ever met with the commander of The Lions unit at any point during your work?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd like to turn your attention to a document which is Rule 65 ter 1D420, with an ERN 1D00-3764, and the Macedonian version is 3763. The English version would be 1D0 -- yes, thank you very much. If I can draw your attention first to the top left-hand corner, you will see it's a document that comes from the Republic of Macedonia, Ministry of Internal Affairs, and it's dated the 3rd of February, 2003. And if you look at the bottom right-hand corner of that document, it's signed by the Minister of the Interior, Hari Kostov. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can draw your attention to the first paragraph of that document, it says this: "Pursuant to Article 55, Item 1 of the law on organisation and work of the bodies of the state administration and with regard to Point 10, Item 2 of the Republic of Macedonia Government's decision for transforming the unit for rapid intervention, Lavovi/Lions [phoen] of the Ministry of Internal Affair of 27 January 2003, the Minister of Interior issued," and then there's a text. My first question, briefly, is were you aware that the Lions unit, the official name of The Lions unit, was Unit for Rapid Intervention?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not. I only knew them as The Lions.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you look at the title of that decision, it says: "Decision for terminating the validity of the decision to form rapid intervention police battalion of the Ministry of Interior Affairs." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you go to the first paragraph below, it says that: "With the entering into force of this decision, the decision to form rapid intervention police battalion of the Ministry of Interior," and then there's a number, it's 16.1-4475 of 6 August 2001, "is being terminated." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that suggests that the rapid intervention police battalion -- Battalion of the Ministry was created by the decision with that number. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, at this stage we'll tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D88, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Although the date of August 6th, we certainly were concerned and aware of a unit called The Lions before that date.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let's look at the next document, then. It's Exhibit P74, ERN 042-4682-80-01 in the English, and it's -- yes. First, if I may ask you to look at the top left-hand corner of that document, again you will see it's a document from the Republic of Macedonia, Ministry of Internal Affairs, and it bears the same number and the same date, that's 16.1-4475/1, and the date is 6th August of 2001. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then there's a bulky paragraph which is essentially the legal basis upon which the decision was taken, and it reads like that: "Based on Article 55, paragraph 1, of the Law on the Organisation of and Work of State Administration and Agencies, Item 2 of the decision of the Government of the Republic of Macedonia to establish a unit for special purposes," and then there's a number of decision -- a number mentioned, and it refers to a decision of the President of the Republic of Macedonia to establish a temporary unit for combat against terrorism of classification ADT number 07-54 of 15/06/2001: "The Minister of Internal Affairs brought the following." Can you see that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it says it's a decision to establish a rapid intervention police battalion of the Ministry of Internal Affairs. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then if I can ask you to turn to the second page of that document, and ask you in particular to focus on what is numbered as paragraph 4 of that document. It says this: "Filling up the rapid intervention police battalion will be made on a voluntary basis and by assignment from the special police unit of the Ministry of Internal Affairs." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It then goes on to say: "Members of the rapid intervention police battalion from the reserve forces of the Ministry of Internal Affairs are employed as full-time employees at the Ministry of Internal Affairs." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: M'mm-hmm, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then it goes on to add: "Members of the rapid intervention police battalions are required to remain in the service for at least three years, starting from the date of assignment to the battalion, that is, from the day the employment agreement is concluded." And then if I may also ask you to look at paragraph 5: "The selection of candidates to fill in the rapid intervention police battalion is performed by a special committee composed of the head of Sector Special Units as the Chairman and to members from the Department of Police." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it's signed by the Minister of Internal Affairs, Ljube Boskoski; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you will agree, I hope, that this is in complete contradiction with the press report which we have referred earlier and which you have adopted in your evidence. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, as I think I've made clear, I'm a human rights investigator not a security expert, and I've also made clear that I'm testifying on the basis of press reports. Due to --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'll just --

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is certainly not the paramilitary Lions unit that we were concerned about, as a human rights organisation. This document may refer to the formalisation, under international pressure, of some of the those irregular units, but in my opinion the date of this document is inconsistent when we first heard about The Lions and their activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you this: This opinion which you've just expressed about a formalisation process, is that again based on press reports, or did you see any particular documents?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's certainly not based on any legal documents. It's based on us following the press reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'll ask you to look at a different document, then. It's Rule 65 ter 222. It's a Defence document, and it has an ERN N000-5388-N000-5404-80. The Macedonian version, Your Honour, will be at N000-5388. Thank you. Sir, this is a list of persons that were employed in the intervention unit -- rapid intervention unit, Lavovi, based on received concurrence, it says, by the Minister of Finance on the 12th of November of 2001, and that is a list that comes from the archives of the Ministry of Interior. Would you agree, sir, that again this document suggests that The Lions unit was, in fact, a formalised police unit of the Ministry of Interior and not some sort of organisation with which Mr. Boskoski had contracts and personal relationships?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the providence of this document. I don't even see the date when the document was issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, the date is 12 November 2001. It's at the top.

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is that the date the document was issued, or is this a review based on the finance documentation that was issued on that date?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, my --

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because as I state in my statement, there was a controversy when this unit was disbanded about their employment contracts, and I assume that this document relates to establishing who exactly was in the unit and who was not. So, I mean, it's very difficult for me to testify about documents that -- whose relevance and nature is unclear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps to assist you, this is a document that was provided to the Defence by the Office of the Prosecution, and we understand it comes directly from the archives of the Ministry of Interior or the Ministry of Finance. Would that assist you?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I understand is after the end of the war, The Lions unit was disbanded. They blockaded some roads, including the main road leading to Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Let's just stay on the question, Mr. Bouckaert, if I may. Would you agree that this list, again, as with the previous document, suggests that there is, in fact, no merit to the allegations reported in the newspaper in which you have reported in your statement as regard The Lions unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see how this document goes to the allegation.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a controversy about the nature of their employment contracts, from what I understand from the press, and I'm sure the government made an attempt to resolve that conflict and to reopen the road. And from what I understand from what this document looks like, is a document listing the final people who had membership in this unit and who required -- who received required compensation so the roads to Kosovo would be reopened.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's not exactly my question, Mr. Bouckaert. In your statement, you claim that after the conflict it became publicly known that The Lions had employment contracts not with the Ministry of Interior but with Mr. Boskoski directly. Is that what you told the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and as I've made clear in my prior testimony, I did raise the categorical language of this paragraph. It was the only paragraph that I discussed with the Prosecutor that I had problems with, because it did not reflect that this was my opinion based on press reports.
