As I've said, from my understanding based on those press reports, the controversy when The Lions unit was disbanded was between claims that they had contracts with the Ministry of Interior or directly with Boskoski, and I see this document as probably finalising an agreement listing who was in this unit and who would receive compensation. So I don't see it inconsistent with my statement, but perhaps, because as I said, I don't have a security expertise, I'm misunderstanding the nature of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps we'll try to stick to your understanding of this matter, Mr. Bouckaert, and I'll ask that the witness be shown 65 ter 1D419. And it's ERN 1D00-3761. And I'll just ask you to focus again perhaps on the top left-hand corner of the document. At the time it's written: "Public of Macedonia, Ministry of Interior Affairs." It has a number and it's dated 22nd of August of 2002. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And there's a big subheader in the middle of the document which says: "Employment Agreement." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you look at the first paragraph of that document, it says the following: "Pursuant to Article 14 of the Law for Employment Relations Official Gazette and Article 12 of the Collective Agreement of the MOI, again Official Gazette, the employer, the Ministry of Interior Affairs of the Republic of Macedonia, represented by the Minister of Interior Affairs and the employee Nikola Strajapolos [phoen], a citizen of the Republic of Macedonia from Tetovo," with address and so on,"made the following ..." And then it says "Employment agreements." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you can look at the third paragraph, it says: "The employee establishes an employment relationship for employment as a police officer at the unit for fast intervention - Lions, in the Department for Police at the MOI of Republic of Macedonia." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then if you can look at paragraph 5 of that document, it says: "The employee accept the responsibilities which are determined by the Law on Employment Relations, the Law on Internal Affairs, the Law for Organisation and Work of the Bodies of the State Authority, the collective agreement, and the acts of the employer, and the separate rights and duties established by the resolution for forming of a police unit for fast intervention - Lion of 6 August 2001, and the rule book for the conditions and the procedure for assigning the rights and duties for members of the unit for fast intervention of the MOI." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that would suggest, doesn't it, that the contracts between members of The Lions unit and the other party was, in fact, with the Ministry of Interior directly; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time that this employment contract in August 2002 was issued, that would be correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, perhaps we would tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D89, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps I will read out to you the evidence of another witness who's testified before this Tribunal. It's Witness M-56, Your Honour, who testified on the 18th of June of 2007. It's at page 2203 to 2204. The witness, Mr. Bouckaert, was asked the following: "Bearing in mind that part of the policemen who are members of the unit Posivna [phoen] already employed with this decision, also it has been determined that one portion of the reserve that will become part of the rapid intervention battalion will be hired, that is to say, employed at the Ministry; is that correct?" "Yes, that's correct." And then the witness was asked: "And if somebody would say before this court that the members of these battalions have been employed or reached the employment directly with the Minister, would not be correct, because the decision clearly says that they are going to be employed by the Ministry of Interior; is that correct?" The witness said: "Yes, that's correct: So you would agree, sir, that this evidence would be directly contradicting the press report in any case on which you based your assertions?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I think as I made very clear in my testimony, we understood that a group called The Lions existed before the establishment of this unit, and this may have been an attempt to regularise this unit which had been formed before, but I don't see it as contradictory to my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But, sir, do you have any evidence of the suggestion which you are now making, that this is merely an attempt to regularise the situation, or is it something that you are simply assuming or claiming?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I base it on the fact that this unit was established on August 6th, 2001, and we certainly had press reports showing the existence of a unit called The Lions talking about their demonstrations and their actions long before then.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But it is not your evidence, sir, that the members of the first unit and the members of the police unit at the time were the same people, or is that what you are claiming today?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm just saying that before this order was issued, there already was some kind of formation called The Lions which was of great concern to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, again, simply to clarify the point fully, those contracts which you claim Mr. Boskoski had with a different Lion outfit, you never see -- you never saw any of those; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You've also made a statement in your report of 5 September of 2001 to the effect that Mr. Boskoski was openly hostile to international actors in Macedonia including Western media, NATO, and the OSCE. Do you recall making that statement?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You also said that Mr. Boskoski was an ultra-nationalist. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you also made a statement that there was a risk that in such climate, nationalist government officials such as Minister Boskoski could use threat of public incitement against the OSCE; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as I had seen during the riots in Skopje during June following the evacuation of NLA fighters by NATO forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And before making that claim, sir, did you contact the high officials of the OSCE to verify whether that was their impression or their view that there was such a risk from Mr. Boskoski?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure they would have denied it, and in their public statements they spoke about -- they certainly never mentioned such tensions.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, are you saying you're sure that they would deny it. Did you talk to any of those officials which claim that they were afraid of Mr. Boskoski's threats?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never spoke to Ambassador Ungaro about it, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you speak to Mr. Seford, his deputy?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Exhibit 1D38? It's an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters ask you to observe the pauses between questions and answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, this is the translation of a letter. The English for you is on the left. It's a translation of a letter actually sent in Macedonian, and it's sent to Mr. Ljube Boskoski, Minister of Interior, and it comes from the deputy head of the OSCE mission in Skopje, Mr. Robin Seford. I'd like to draw your attention to first the date, 14th of June, 2001, and to the first paragraph of this letter. It says: "Please allow me to express my deepest personal gratitude and respect and that of the OSCE mission for the exceptional level of understanding, cooperation, readiness and efficiency which you and all the members of your valued Ministry have always demonstrated during our mutual contact. The permits given by the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Macedonia to our personnel, international and local, are of critical importance for the work and functioning of the office of the OSCE mission in the Republic of Macedonia in accordance with our mandate." You will agree, I hope, Mr. Bouckaert, that this does not suggest the thought of threats or concern which you expressed in your report; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It reflects the usual diplomatic language which is used in such letters.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, are you able to state before this Trial Chamber, then, that you know that Mr. Seford was being merely diplomatic or was that just your opinion?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it also correct, sir, that a great part of your reports and many of your findings in your report are based solely on press reports; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, would it be correct to say a third and a quarter of all references in your reports are to press reports and media outlets; would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just because we cite a lot of media reports to support certain statements in our report does not mean that it's based, in your words, that many of our findings are based solely on press reports, no. The findings as to the crimes that were committed in Ljuboten are based on our interviews, on our visit to Ljuboten, and our discussions with various other observers.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let's just stick with my question, if you may for a second. Is that correct that approximately one-third to one-quarter of your references, and that would be approximately 20 footnotes of about 70, were to press reports or media outlets? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and almost all of those are focused on our discussion of the role of the OSCE and other issues, not our own investigation into the events in Ljuboten on August 10th to 12th.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, isn't that the case that the only reference you make to the presence of Mr. Boskoski in the area at the time, as discussed earlier, is to a media report to that effect and a video?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we've gone over this in great detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, this has been asked and answered extensively.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It is reaching that point, Mr. Mettraux. Have you got any further specific --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'll will move on this point, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct, Mr. Bouckaert, that all of your findings concerning the events of Ljubotenski Bacila, which in your view were the cause or the lead-up to what happened in Ljuboten, solely based on media reports?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: We do not say that this is the cause of what happened in Ljuboten. The incident of what happened prior to the attack on Ljuboten is based on information from the official state media, yes, of the official Macedonian information agency, I should say.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But is that correct that you make the claim in your reports, and I believe also in a number of media reports, that the incident of Ljuboten was in revenge for what had happened in Ljubotenski Bacila; is that the finding you've made?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that your finding in relation to what happened in Ljubotenski Bacila are based solely on media reports?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it also correct that the claim that you make of an attack on the Ljubotens police -- Ljubotenski police station by the NLA on 12th of August 2001 is also based solely on media reports?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they're based on information from the Macedonia Information Agency, which is a state news agency, so we saw them as official releases from the government to that extent.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And again am I correct to understand that you did not seek to verify either this matter or the matter which related to the Ljubotenski Bacila incident?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're talking about the mine explosion?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because we didn't feel the facts related to this incident were in dispute.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: In your statement, you've indicated to the Prosecution that you believed that Mr. Boskoski had called up a significant number of reservists to supplement, I believe is the expression, the regular police. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: There had been a call-up of reservists, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it is your evidence that this call-up was made by Mr. Boskoski; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I believe, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And was that belief based again on press reports?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was based on my general monitoring of the situation at the time. There certainly was a call-up of reservists at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what you refer to by "my general monitoring," would that be monitoring -- and I'm referring to what you say was a call-up made by Mr. Boskoski, this information you received from the press; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't recall exactly, but we attended a variety of meetings with other monitors on a regular basis. We monitored the press. We stayed in close contact with a variety of journalists and diplomats and other observers. So it will be based on a combination of those sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you have any knowledge or awareness of the laws and regulations which apply to this matter, to the calling of reservists from the police?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not directly. I mean, the only point which was of interest to us is that reservists had been called up and were participating in some of these operations and that there were concerns about discipline among those reservists.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And are you aware of the fact that the call-up of police reservists was made at the request or at the behest of the Prime Minister or the President? At any stage, did you become aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that's quite possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, there's a particular document that I would like to show you, Your Honour, but at the discretion of the Chamber, if the Chamber wants to continue for another five minutes. Thank you. It's Rule 65 ter 1D439.1, and it has an ERN of 1D00-4038. And the Macedonian equivalent would be 1D00-4035. Sir, this is essentially a summary of press releases and press reports which were prepared within the Ministry of Interior at the time. It's dated 29th of June, it should be the 29th, it's the 29th of June, 2001, and if I can draw your attention to the second paragraph, which starts with the words: "Demobilisation." Can you see that? It's in the middle of the page. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It says: "Demobilisation of the reserve composition. The Ministry of Interior Affairs, Ljube Boskoski, at the press conference stated, the members of the reserve composition of the Republic of Macedonia will be demobilised and withdrawn from the check-points around Skopje, with the aim of allowing politicians to continue with the peaceful solving of the problem. They will again be engaged when the President will determine that they are needed for defending the country. I am doing this because of the series of accusations by the opposition and by the Social Democratic Union of Macedonia directed at me that I'm being radical, that I'm for war, that I want to conduct a police upheaval, that I am for mobilisation of the reserve composition of the police, according to party criteria, and that I am 'stopping' the realisation of President Trajkovski's plan for peaceful resolution of the crisis." And then the next paragraph say: "I deny all of the accusations and categorically claim that am for peace in this region, but for rightful peace. I personally think that there is no single reason for me to defend myself from the accusations according to which the MOI and the Minister are responsible, also for the events that occurred in front of the Macedonian Parliament, because at that moment I was the only person who stood before the Macedonian people and tried to calm the gathered crowd of people." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'll just ask the Registry to show the next document which relates to the present one. It's Rule 65 ter 1D439.2 with an ERN 1D00-4042 in the English and 4040 in the Macedonian. It would be the next page in the Macedonian version, please. Mr. Bouckaert, I'll ask you to look at the last of the three sections of that document. As you can see, it's dated the 13th of June, so that's the next day. And if it could be enlarged a bit for Mr. Bouckaert, please. It says the following: "The police reservists are returning to the check-points. The Ministry of Interior Affairs withdrew the decision for demobilisation of the police reserve composition and ordered remobilisation which will be processed selectively. The remobilisation of the police reserve composition is conducted upon a request of the commander-in-chief of the Macedonian armed forces, Boris Trajkovski, due to the actual security situation in the country." Were you aware of that information, Mr. Bouckaert, at the time?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'll seek to tender these two documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, they will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 1D439.1 will become Exhibit 1D90, and 65 ter 1D439.2 will become Exhibit 1D91, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would that be a convenient time, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mettraux. Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have a matter of scheduling that I must raise, and since I cannot speak directly with the witness, I may respectfully ask the Chamber to consider whether it needs to communicate with Mr. Bouckaert. Before this session began, counsel for Mr. Boskoski told me that it's very possible that my colleague will take the entire day -- the entire court day tomorrow with continued cross-examination. That would leave Thursday -- part of Thursday for perhaps additional cross-examination by Mr. Apostolski and some redirect examination by the Prosecution. It's my understanding that this witness is presently scheduled to fly back to his current place of work and residence on Thursday, and I simply don't know whether the passage of time is going to effect this witness or his ability to remain here through Thursday and perhaps not until Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Let me start with you, Mr. Mettraux. Your time estimate?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, first we would like to indicate that we would, as far as possible, try to arrange it for the witness as well and that we will seek to be as short as possible. Mr. Saxon is correct, we believe we will need certainly the entire day of tomorrow and possibly another session of the day after. We will try to, during the evening and tomorrow morning, to shorten the cross-examination, the further cross-examination. I would simply point out, Your Honour, if I may, that in effect the cross-examination is a cross-examination of evidence which is at least the equivalent of four days of court time, as a minimum, since Mr. Bouckaert was interviewed, I understand, for three days by the Prosecution and that he was examined in chief or partly in chief for a day and a bit, simply to indicate that we will try to be as quick as we can also for the witness and for the rest of the scheduling. This is our estimate at this stage, perhaps one day and one session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I support what my colleague Mettraux just said, and I would also like to inform the Court that this evening we will have a meeting with our colleagues from the Defence of Mr. Boskoski. Therefore, jointly we can make this as short as possible, the cross-examination, to make it as short as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's not a very helpful estimate, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I know this. However, I believe that in the course of tomorrow and the first break in the course of tomorrow would perhaps be a more probable time to say, if my colleague Mettraux finishes by tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bouckaert, your travel commitments, can they accommodate being here on Thursday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe I'm scheduled to fly out on Thursday evening, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you know at what time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think the flight leaves at about 8.00 or 9.00 p.m., but I can confirm that. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Because we are scheduled to sit from 2.15 to 7.00 on Thursday.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe in order to catch that flight, I would probably have to finish sometime before the final session on Thursday, but if the Defence needs me, I will change my travel plans, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Bouckaert, we're grateful for your position and attitude in the matter. It takes the pressure off the immediate problem, but not the general problem. We have two days allowed for this witness. He's going to run four to five days, which is exactly the problem we had with Mr. Hutsch at the end of last week. It's simply going to have to speed up. People will have to be more selective of what is material and more quick in dealing with it. And to that end, Mr. Mettraux, we would encourage you to do all that is possible to finish by the end of tomorrow. And with that then done, Mr. Apostolski and Mr. Saxon may be able to finish in time to allow Mr. Bouckaert to catch his scheduled flight, and we'll see by the end of tomorrow whether that can be achieved on Thursday. So if all counsel will be aware that the Chamber has indicated at the end of last week that it's going to have to become more positive in its time allowances, because we can't just let this pattern continue to develop of far longer times spent with each witness. But for the moment, Mr. Mettraux, we'd be grateful for you, over the evening, to do all that can be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It will be done, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. That leaves you at a state of some uncertainty, Mr. Bouckaert. You may be able to explore the possibility of getting a tentative booking or something like that, but what can be done will be done to get you free by about 6.00 on Thursday.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I appreciate that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will now adjourn and we resume tomorrow at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: 6.50 p.m., to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 4th day of July, 2007, at 2.15 p.m. 25
